name: Environment Portability
intent: Rewrite or explain commands so they work across shells, operating systems, and path conventions.

source.text: When a command depends on shell or OS behavior, identify the platform difference, provide a portable alternative, and include a verification step.

inputs.description: A command, package script, or failure caused by shell or OS differences.

outputs.description: A portable alternative with explanation and verification.

steps.title: Identify platform difference
steps.description: Find the shell, path, quoting, environment variable, or command availability difference.

steps.title: Provide portable alternative
steps.description: Propose a command or script pattern that avoids the platform-specific failure.

steps.title: Verify portability
steps.description: Name a test, dry run, or command to verify the alternative.

rules.sourceText: Explain which platform or shell behavior caused the problem.
rules.normalizedForm: The response names the relevant platform or shell difference.

rules.sourceText: Prefer portable alternatives over one-off shell-specific workarounds.
rules.normalizedForm: The response provides a portable or cross-platform alternative.

tools.name: shell
tools.purpose: Inspect or run commands when available.

platformNotes.linux: Use POSIX shell conventions unless the task says otherwise.
platformNotes.macos: BSD userland behavior may differ from GNU tools.
platformNotes.windows: PowerShell uses different environment variable and command chaining syntax.

environment.description: Shell syntax and command availability vary across Linux, macOS, Windows, WSL, and containers.

checks.name: Platform difference stated
checks.assertion: The response names a shell or OS difference.

checks.name: Portable alternative stated
checks.assertion: The response includes a portable or cross-platform alternative.

checks.name: Verification step stated
checks.assertion: The response includes a way to verify the command.
